algorithm: Perform a depth-first search (DFS) on the graph to identify articulation points
For each node, track the discovery time and low-link values
A node is an articulation point if it has a child in the DFS tree whose low-link value is greater than or equal to the discovery time of the node
Return the list of articulation points in ascending order by vertex index
constraints: Edges are distinct and undirected (given as [u,v] with u < v)
Articulation points must be returned as strings in ascending order
edge_cases: Graph with a single vertex (n=1) has no articulation points
Graph with no edges (n>=2) has all vertices as articulation points
Graph that is biconnected has no articulation points
Graph with multiple connected components: articulation points are identified per component
parsed.inputs: n: integer >= 1; edges: list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n
parsed.output: Ascending list of articulation vertices (as strings) across all connected components
parsed.purpose: Yield the articulation points (cut vertices) of a graph constructed from integer vertices 0 to n-1 and distinct undirected edges
